raw_response:
Okay, let me think this through the way I do every spring, sitting on the kang with my wife and going over what we'll do this year.

---

I'm 61 now. My wife and I have been working these 18 mu since before our kids were grown. The kids work outside now — our son drives a truck, our daughter-in-law works in town — so it's mostly the two of us in the fields. When cotton picking comes in the fall, the family comes back to help, and if we're really behind I pay a few neighbors by the day.

**Splitting the land.** Like always, I keep about 12 mu in cotton on the sandier ground out west — cotton is what pays, it's what my father grew, it's what I know. The other 6 mu near the village I keep in wheat-maize, two crops a year. That gives us our flour and some corn for ourselves and to sell. You can't live on just cotton. If the cotton price drops — and it does, every few years — at least we have grain in the shed.

**Wheat (6 mu, already in the ground).** I planted it in early October, Jimai variety, same seed the agricultural station sells everybody. I put down two bags of compound fertilizer per mu before plowing — that's the base. Right now it's April, so the wheat is jointing. I already gave it water once when it turned green after winter, and I topdressed urea with that — maybe 15 kg per mu, a full scoop and a bit more. I'll irrigate one more time before heading, maybe again at filling if it doesn't rain. That's three waters total, which is what everyone around here does. Harvest first week of June if the weather holds.

**Maize (6 mu, goes in after wheat).** Right after the combine leaves the wheat field, I'll run the rotary tiller and plant maize the same week — no time to waste, the season is tight. Zhengdan hybrid, whatever the agro-shop has this year. I buy new seed every year for maize, you can't save hybrid seed. I put compound fertilizer with the planter and topdress urea at the big-trumpet stage, about 15 kg per mu. If the rains come, I don't irrigate; if July is dry, I give it one water from the well. Pumping costs money so I don't do it unless I have to. Harvest late September.

**Cotton (12 mu, the big job).** This is where my money goes in and where it comes out. I plant around April 20, plus or minus a few days depending on the soil temperature — when I can stand barefoot on the field without shivering, it's time. I use film mulch like everyone — keeps the soil warm, holds moisture, keeps weeds down. Before planting I put down compound fertilizer and a bit of urea, maybe 12 kg N per mu total across the season, most of it at base with some topdress at squaring. Cotton doesn't like too much nitrogen or it grows tall and doesn't set bolls — my father used to say "a fat cotton plant is a poor cotton plant."

The headache with cotton is the bugs. Bollworm, aphids, spider mites — I spray maybe five or six times through the season, whatever the agro-shop man recommends when I go in. It's expensive but without spraying you get nothing. I irrigate twice from the well, once at squaring and once at flowering if it's dry. Picking starts in September and runs through October — three or four picks. That's when I need the family home and maybe hire two or three days of help.

**About the money.** Cash is tight in spring before anything sells. The wheat won't give me income until June. I buy fertilizer on credit from the agro-shop and pay him back after cotton sells in the fall — he knows me, I've been buying from him twenty years. I don't spend on anything fancy. Same seeds, same fertilizers, same routine. If it worked last year and the year before, it'll work this year.

**What I'm watching this year.** Cotton price was okay last fall, not great. If the price at the gin drops more, next year I might put another mu or two into maize instead. But for this year, same plan as always.
